question: After removing within-layer expert reloads, how much old-generation delay remains from a new prefill, and does smaller prefill work reduce it at a complete-request benefit or only shift the wait?
scope: one controlled event-arrival diagnostic; strongest measured expert grouping substrate; no new controller or novelty claim
runtime: vLLM0.26 eager Triton BF16, WiSP LRU fixedcap24, expert-major disjoint groups

new.arrival: host receipt of fourth output from both old requests

requests.source: first three existing prepared/short WikiText documents; shared calibration inputs, not independent document holdout

actions.hold: same virtual boundary snapshot, do not submit new request; only direct interference negative control
actions.chunk8: add new request, set prefill threshold8 at boundary
actions.chunk128: add new request, set prefill threshold128 at boundary

prefix: all arms use threshold32 and identical two-old execution before action; compare complete slots/map/LRU, KV logical blocks/free, old output prefix and computed counters. Logical state equality is not a KV tensor bitwise claim.
warmup: same initial one-request/two-output warmup, then expert injection8 then expert injection128 in every fresh process; prefix threshold32 reset before each episode; all raw retained; check measured shapes occurred in warmup
execution_checks: each live old decode advances one token per engine call
third request is submitted exactly once after both old outputs equal4
each expert call loads its own initial missing experts once
full input-output/request and physical-row alignment; no trace reuse across actions
timing: event arrival is the old fourth-token receipt, before snapshot/callback; observation and action overhead remain in old ITL and new TTFT. Record explicit engine.step start/end and scheduler step indices. Warmup and validation costs kept separate.
primary_metrics: actual expert payload and unique-entry lower bound
post-action decode cost and final logical cache
retention: all attempts and repeats retained, no selection by outcome
continue: Use measured cost decomposition to choose one simple next action/execution refinement; a failed threshold does not falsify the problem.
stop_to_diagnose: semantic/identity failure or incomplete old progression, missing event, wrong action effect or resource mismatch invalidates corresponding measurement.
claim_ceiling: single GPU controlled-cap OLMoE event injection; no production SLO, natural-arrival capacity, general task-quality or true out-of-HBM deployment claim
next: One adjustment determined by the measured dominant residual; do not add a predictor before checking ordinary length/queue and decode execution cost.
